[6, 8] In the week leading up to its expiration, the contract's price fluctuated within the 19-20 cents per pound range. [7] On its final day of trading, the contract closed at 20.3 cents per pound. [7] Market analysis published on July 1, 2024, confirmed these events, noting that both commercial participants and speculators were active as the contract expired. [7] <2> On June 25, 2024, the raw sugar futures market was observed trading within the 18-19c/lb range ahead of the July 2024 futures contract expiration, a consequential event in the sugar market. [2] The contract officially expired on June 28, 2024. [6] This event was monitored to see if it would alter the prevailing downward price trend of 2024. [2] In the week of the expiry, the market saw a slight upward movement, trading between 19-20c/lb and closing near 20.3c/lb. [3] The expiry is a significant event as it is one of the few times the futures and physical markets align, and this instance saw over 1 million tonnes of raw sugar delivered. [4] <3> A USDA analysis of the U.S. Drought Monitor report from June 4, 2024, indicated that 100% of Florida's sugarcane areas were experiencing drought conditions. This was broken down into 26% of the cane area being in a state of severe drought and 74% in moderate drought, which raised concerns for the crop. A separate USDA report published on June 18, 2024, referenced a U.S. Drought Monitor analysis as of June 11, which stated 78 percent of the area was in severe drought and 22 percent in moderate drought, leading to a reduction in Florida's 2024/25 sugar output forecast. <4> Sucro Limited, an integrated sugar refiner serving North American markets, announced its financial results for the first quarter ending March 31, 2024. This revenue was generated from sugar deliveries totaling 182,865 metric tons, also a new quarterly record. Additionally, Sucro confirmed the completion of $20.3 million in debt financing to support its new refinery project in Hamilton, Ontario. <5> On May 20, 2024, the raw sugar futures market (No. 11) saw prices decline to trade in the range of 18-19 cents per pound, with the market closing at 18.1 cents per pound on the preceding Friday. [1] This decrease in price prompted end-users to significantly increase their long positions by 11,400 lots. [1] In contrast, producers did not add to their hedges and instead reduced their short positions by closing out 7,200 lots. [1] <6> The USDA's Economic Research Service released its Sugar and Sweeteners Outlook on May 16, 2024. In the report, the 2023/24 U.S. sugar supply forecast was reduced, with production lowered by 84,000 short tons, raw value (STRV), to 9.131 million due to decreases in both beet and cane sugar output. For the 2024/25 fiscal year, the initial production forecast is set at 9.232 million STRV, anticipating increases for both sugar types. The outlook also adjusted import figures for 2023/24, raising them by 21,000 STRV to 3.438 million, while forecasting 2024/25 imports at 3.028 million STRV. The report provided these initial projections for the 2024/25 supply and demand as part of the broader World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates (WASDE). <7> In its May 2024 World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates (WASDE) report, the USDA released its initial forecast for the 2024/25 season, projecting U.S. sugar production to reach 9.23 million short tons (ST). This represents an increase from the 9.13 million ST produced in the 2023/24 season. The anticipated growth is attributed to increased output from both beet and cane sugar farmers. Specifically, beet sugar production for 2024/25 is projected at 5.111 million ST, while cane sugar is forecast at 4.121 million ST. As a consequence of the higher domestic production, the USDA projects that sugar imports for the 2024/25 season will decrease by 410,000 ST to 3.02 million ST. <8> During the week of March 25, 2024, raw sugar futures (No. 11) were observed to be trading sideways, holding steady at a price of 21 cents per pound. This period of stable pricing coincided with a continued lack of significant participation from speculators, who have largely maintained a net neutral position in the market following a notable price collapse in December 2023. <9> The USDA, in its World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates (WASDE) report of March 8, 2024, announced a reduction in the forecast for the 2023/24 domestic sugar production. [4] The forecast was lowered by 109,050 short tons, raw value (STRV), primarily due to a significant decrease in beet sugar production. [4] This reduction was attributed to warmer-than-average temperatures in the Upper Midwest, specifically the Red River Valley and Michigan, which led to increased beet pile shrink. [4] The winter of 2023-2024 was the warmest on record for the Midwest, with persistent warmth throughout December 2023 and February 2024. [5, 7, 8] The March WASDE report indicated that an increase in Florida's cane sugar production mostly offset a small reduction in Texas. [4] However, Louisiana and Texas did experience a severe to exceptional 'flash drought' that began in the late summer and persisted through the fall of 2023, impacting the sugarcane crop. [14]

Prediction target period: from 2025-06-24 to 2025-07-09. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> In a biannual report released on May 22, 2025, the USDA projected a record global sugar production for the 2025/26 season, forecasting a 4.7% year-over-year increase to 189.318 million metric tons. The report also anticipated that global ending stocks would climb by 7.5% to 41.188 million metric tons. This forecast of a significant global surplus, driven by expected production increases in Brazil and India, exerted downward pressure on sugar prices. Following the report, New York sugar futures fell to a 4.25-year low, and London sugar prices dropped to a 4-year low. <2> In a report published on April 23, 2025, it was confirmed that U.S. sugar prices declined during the week ending April 17, 2025, driven by a combination of weak demand and significant oversupply. The price drop was influenced by sluggish trading and slow deliveries. Processors sought to reduce burdensome inventories, with refined sugar stocks at the end of February recorded as the second highest on record and up approximately 13% from the previous year. Consequently, spot beet sugar prices in the Midwest fell by 1 to 3 cents per pound, and refined cane sugar prices for the 2025 calendar year were lowered by 1 cent per pound in all regions. <3> Sucro Limited, an integrated sugar refiner, announced its financial results for the fourth quarter and full year ended December 31, 2024. [1] The report provides a retrospective overview of the company's performance. The company noted that an increase in adjusted gross profit for the quarter was driven by higher volumes from favorable world market sugar deliveries in the last quarter of 2024. [1] <4> The National Confectioners Association (NCA) released its 2025 "State of Treating" report on March 3, 2025. The report revealed that U.S. confectionery sales reached a record $54.2 billion in 2024. This sales growth occurred despite consumer concerns over grocery prices, with 98% of shoppers still purchasing confectionery products during the year. Chocolate remained the largest segment, accounting for $28.1 billion in sales. However, non-chocolate candy demonstrated significant growth, with sales reaching $21.7 billion. Looking ahead, the NCA projects that total U.S. confectionery sales will surpass $70 billion by 2029, indicating continued strong demand for these products. <5> In February 2025, food technology company Oobli, which has developed a sweet protein platform, announced a partnership with global ingredient solutions provider Ingredion. [3, 5] The collaboration is designed to scale and commercialize Oobli's sweet protein-based sugar alternatives by combining them with Ingredion's portfolio of natural sweeteners, such as stevia, to create enhanced, healthier sweetener systems for the food and beverage industry. [2, 3] This move responds to the growing consumer demand for healthier, low-sugar products. [1] The partnership followed successful co-development trials and positive consumer feedback on products blending the two companies' ingredients. [3] The announcement coincided with Oobli securing $18 million in Series B1 funding, with Ingredion Ventures participating as a new investor. [2, 6] This also came after Oobli received FDA GRAS "no questions" letters for two of its sweet proteins, monellin and brazzein, confirming their safety for use in food and beverages. [4, 5] <6> A market report on February 5, 2025, indicated that contracting for the 2025-26 U.S. sugar season was proceeding slowly due to a significant price disparity between buyers and sellers. Sellers were holding their offers steady with the previous season's prices, around 45¢ to 48¢ per pound, citing uncertainties as the 2025 crop had not yet been planted. In contrast, buyers' bids were in the lower 40¢ per pound range, influenced by ample domestic sugar supplies, steady demand, and raw sugar futures prices that were well below year-ago levels. <7> In January 2025, the growing use of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs introduced significant uncertainty into the U.S. sugar market, causing food manufacturers to become reluctant to enter into supply contracts for the 2025-26 period. Reports indicated that the increased adoption of these drugs was beginning to curb overall consumer spending on food, with sugar consumption likely to be impacted. This uncertainty about future product demand led to a slowdown in contract negotiations, as buyers hesitated to commit, choosing instead to wait and see if their sales would meet expectations before securing sugar supplies. <8> The FAO Food Price Index for December 2024, announced on January 3, 2025, registered a 5.1% decrease in the sugar price index from November, averaging 120.0 points for the month. The drop in world sugar prices was primarily attributed to larger-than-expected sugar production in Brazil during the second half of November. Improved crop prospects in other key producing nations also contributed to the decline. <9> The sugarcane harvest in Florida and Louisiana during the fourth quarter of 2024 was affected by hurricanes in late September and early October. In Florida, Hurricane Helene made landfall on September 26, followed by Hurricane Milton on October 9. [13, 14, 17] The storms impacted over 5.7 million acres of agricultural land in Florida, including sugarcane regions. [14, 17] The industry was hit at an inopportune time just weeks before harvest, with winds causing stalks to bend or break, a condition known as lodging, which complicates mechanical harvesting and can reduce yields. [2, 4] In Louisiana, a different storm, Hurricane Francine, made landfall on September 11 and caused damage to the sugarcane crop in the southeastern part of the state, including lodging and root breakage, which negatively affected sucrose accumulation. [12, 15] Despite these challenges, which caused sugar recovery in affected areas to be below normal, the overall 2024 Louisiana harvest was successful, setting records for the total amount of cane processed due to an increase in acreage and good growing conditions in other parts of the state. [12, 15]

Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> A series of crop health reports from July 2025, utilizing Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) readings, indicated contrasting outlooks for sugar beet yields in key U.S. states. Minnesota and Idaho were both flagged for potentially diminished yields. In Minnesota, lower than typical NDVI readings were attributed to excessive rain and flooding, which led to an estimated loss of +-4,000 acres. In Idaho, a decrease in NDVI readings compared to the long-term average was compounded by issues with Rhizoctonia brought on by heat and the increasing presence of herbicide-resistant weeds. [1, 5] FDA Commissioner Martin Makary stated that advances in food science and consumer protection have rendered many of these standards unnecessary and that they can stifle innovation and the creation of healthier food choices. These issues were heavily exacerbated by escalating raw material costs, specifically multi-decade highs in cocoa and sugar prices, with sugar costs driven up by supply constraints and export limits in India and Thailand. The company pursued an expedited bankruptcy hearing to determine whether it could restructure its debt and maintain operations through the holiday season or face liquidation. <2> A report from October 3, 2025, highlighted worsening dry conditions ahead of the 2025 harvest season, particularly impacting the lower Ohio and Mississippi River areas. Mike Clay, a hydrologics and hydrology branch chief with the Memphis Engineer District, described a "flash drought" over the Ohio Valley and near its confluence with the Mississippi River at Cairo, Illinois. This followed weeks of minimal rain, culminating in the driest August over the Ohio Basin in the last 131 years. Separately, a forecast webinar on August 28, 2025, suggested a risk for an earlier-than-normal first frost for the upper Midwest and Great Lakes region due to the potential for strong cold fronts. <3> In early October 2025, reports confirmed that global sugar prices had fallen significantly during September, reaching multi-year lows. The FAO's Sugar Price Index for September hit its lowest point since March 2021. Specifically, New York raw sugar futures dropped to a five-year low, while London sugar reached a 4.75-year low. Prices for raw sugar futures were reported to have settled around 15.6 cents/lb in early September. This downturn was primarily driven by the outlook for a robust global sugar surplus for the 2025/26 season. Multiple analysts revised their surplus forecasts, with projections including 8.7 MMT from Czarnikow, 10.5 MMT from BMI Group, and 4.1 MMT from Covrig Analytics. The optimistic supply forecasts stemmed from major producers: Brazil's crop forecasting agency, Conab, increased its 2025/26 production estimate to 45 MMT; India's Sugar Mill Association raised its forecast to 31 MMT following strong monsoon rains; and the Thai Sugar Millers Corp projected a 5% year-over-year increase in its 2025/26 crop. <4> Trade data from the Brazilian Food Industry Association (ABIA) revealed that Brazil's sugar exports to the United States plummeted by 69.5% in August 2025 compared to the previous month. This sharp decline was a direct consequence of a new 50% tariff imposed by the U.S. government on a range of Brazilian products, including sugar. The tariff, which consisted of a 40% increase on top of a pre-existing 10% tariff, was announced via an Executive Order on July 30, 2025, and took effect on August 6, 2025. The significant drop in August exports was exacerbated by a likely surge in shipments in July as companies moved to export their products before the new surcharge was implemented. The U.S. government stated the tariffs were a response to allegations of censorship of U.S. companies by Brazilian authorities. <5> In September 2025, analysis of the sugar futures market revealed a strong bearish sentiment as speculators accumulated their largest net-short position since November 2019, reaching -182,608 lots. In Minnesota, lower than typical NDVI readings were attributed to excessive rain and flooding, which led to an estimated loss of +-4,000 acres. In Idaho, a decrease in NDVI readings compared to the long-term average was compounded by issues with Rhizoctonia brought on by heat and the increasing presence of herbicide-resistant weeds. [1, 5] FDA Commissioner Martin Makary stated that advances in food science and consumer protection have rendered many of these standards unnecessary and that they can stifle innovation and the creation of healthier food choices. [1, 2, 4] The initiative aims to modernize food standards, eliminate outdated regulations, and provide the food industry with greater flexibility for production and honest labeling. [3, 5, 6] Companies are advised to assess their product lines to determine if they are impacted by these changes. [3] While the crop was reported to be progressing well and was 7 to 10 days ahead of the previous year, it faced several challenges. [3] Variable rainfall was a key factor, with some areas receiving adequate rain while excessive moisture in other locations flooded low spots, leading to lost acreage. [3] Growers also contended with herbicide-resistant weeds, including glyphosate-resistant kochia, Palmer amaranth, and waterhemp, which in some cases required manual removal. [3] Additionally, fungicide applications for Cercospora leaf spot were underway in multiple regions as the disease had been confirmed. [3] Specifically, the Southern Minnesota Beet Sugar Cooperative anticipated a loss of approximately 4,000 acres due to flooding from excessive rain. [3] <10> The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) has implemented a new policy for the fiscal year 2026, which begins on October 1, 2025, setting the import quota for duty-free specialty sugar, including organic sugar, to the World Trade Organization (WTO) minimum of 1,656 metric tons. This is a significant reduction from the 210,000 metric tons permitted in the previous fiscal year. Consequently, all organic sugar imports beyond this minimal amount will be subjected to high out-of-quota duties. The USDA stated this decision was made to protect domestic sugar production, as sugar imports have more than doubled over the last 20 years. The Organic Trade Association (OTA) predicts this change will lead to an estimated $85 million in new tariff costs and could cause the price of organic sugar to increase by an average of 30%. This has raised concerns among food and beverage manufacturers who rely on imported organic sugar, as over 90% of the organic sugar used in the U.S. is imported and there is only one domestic producer, supplying less than 8% of the demand.

metadata.original_text: This time series records sugar USD Lbs data in the Commodity market price domain, with a collection frequency of daily, focusing on monitoring and analyzing relevant indicators. Prediction target period: from 2025-12-10 to 2025-12-26. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> On December 9, 2025, the USDA released its December World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates (WASDE) report. The report indicated steady U.S. sugar production, as production increases in Louisiana and Florida offset lower beet sugar output caused by higher shrink rates. Conversely, domestic sugar deliveries for consumption are forecast to be slightly lower, including a 32,000 STRV cut in food deliveries, due to ongoing demand weakness. <2> On December 1, 2025, U.S. Customs and Border Protection published Quota Bulletin 26-104, establishing that the 2026 CAFTA-DR Tariff Rate Quotas for agriculture products, including sugar and sugar-containing products, will officially open to importers on January 2, 2026. The quotas will operate under a first-come, first-served processing system, with entries submitted prior to 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time on the opening date treated as 8:30 a.m. entries and prorated if the total exceeds the quota limit. <3> In November 2025, U.S. spot sugar prices experienced a notable decline, with Midwest beet sugar prices dropping by 2 cents/lb at the lower end to approach 48 cents/lb. This downward pricing pressure was driven by sluggish domestic demand—exacerbated by tightening SNAP regulations and the rising use of GLP-1 weight-loss medications—as well as unusually warm weather posing risks to sugar beet quality and storage. Furthermore, prices were heavily influenced by a spillover effect from high global surplus forecasts, with expectations of a world surplus of 1.625 million metric tons for the 2025-26 marketing year pressing on the market. <4> On November 10, 2025, raw sugar futures in New York experienced a significant bounce from five-year lows, climbing 1.8% to 14.36 cents per pound amid short covering and global supply concerns. <5> Monster Beverage Corporation announced record net sales for the third quarter of 2025, driven by strong international sales and increasing consumer demand for sugar-free energy drinks. The company's net sales for Q3 rose 16.8% to $2.20 billion. The Monster Energy® Drinks segment, which includes brands like Monster Energy®, Reign Total Body Fuel®, and others, saw a 17.7% increase in net sales to $2.03 billion for the quarter. Net sales to customers outside of the United States saw a significant increase of 23.3%, reaching $937.1 million. <6> On October 24, 2025, U.S.-based online confectionery wholesaler CandyWarehouse filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of Texas. The Sugar Land, Texas-based company attributed its financial collapse to shifting consumer preferences, post-pandemic challenges, and tight margins across the supply chain. These issues were heavily exacerbated by escalating raw material costs, specifically multi-decade highs in cocoa and sugar prices, with sugar costs driven up by supply constraints and export limits in India and Thailand. The company pursued an expedited bankruptcy hearing to determine whether it could restructure its debt and maintain operations through the holiday season or face liquidation. <7> A report from October 3, 2025, highlighted worsening dry conditions ahead of the 2025 harvest season, particularly impacting the lower Ohio and Mississippi River areas. Mike Clay, a hydrologics and hydrology branch chief with the Memphis Engineer District, described a "flash drought" over the Ohio Valley and near its confluence with the Mississippi River at Cairo, Illinois. This followed weeks of minimal rain, culminating in the driest August over the Ohio Basin in the last 131 years. Separately, a forecast webinar on August 28, 2025, suggested a risk for an earlier-than-normal first frost for the upper Midwest and Great Lakes region due to the potential for strong cold fronts. <8> In early October 2025, reports confirmed that global sugar prices had fallen significantly during September, reaching multi-year lows. The FAO's Sugar Price Index for September hit its lowest point since March 2021. Specifically, New York raw sugar futures dropped to a five-year low, while London sugar reached a 4.75-year low. Prices for raw sugar futures were reported to have settled around 15.6 cents/lb in early September. This downturn was primarily driven by the outlook for a robust global sugar surplus for the 2025/26 season. Multiple analysts revised their surplus forecasts, with projections including 8.7 MMT from Czarnikow, 10.5 MMT from BMI Group, and 4.1 MMT from Covrig Analytics. The optimistic supply forecasts stemmed from major producers: Brazil's crop forecasting agency, Conab, increased its 2025/26 production estimate to 45 MMT; India's Sugar Mill Association raised its forecast to 31 MMT following strong monsoon rains; and the Thai Sugar Millers Corp projected a 5% year-over-year increase in its 2025/26 crop. <9> Trade data from the Brazilian Food Industry Association (ABIA) revealed that Brazil's sugar exports to the United States plummeted by 69.5% in August 2025 compared to the previous month. This sharp decline was a direct consequence of a new 50% tariff imposed by the U.S. government on a range of Brazilian products, including sugar. The tariff, which consisted of a 40% increase on top of a pre-existing 10% tariff, was announced via an Executive Order on July 30, 2025, and took effect on August 6, 2025. The significant drop in August exports was exacerbated by a likely surge in shipments in July as companies moved to export their products before the new surcharge was implemented. The U.S. government stated the tariffs were a response to allegations of censorship of U.S. companies by Brazilian authorities. <10> In September 2025, analysis of the sugar futures market revealed a strong bearish sentiment as speculators accumulated their largest net-short position since November 2019, reaching -182,608 lots. As prices moved lower, commercial end-users took advantage of the situation to extend their cover, adding nearly 31,000 long positions. This activity caused the net commercial position to become net-long for the first time since 2019.
